title: Subtree Counts and the Maximum Mean Subtree Order
summary: For a finite simple graph $G$ of positive order, let $s_k(G)$ be the number of its $k$-vertex tree subgraphs. We prove that, among graphs of a fixed order $n$, the ratios $s_k(G)/s_k(K_n)$ form a nonincreasing sequence in $k$. It follows that the complete graph maximizes the mean subtree order: $μ(G)\leqμ(K_n)$, with equality if and only if $G$ is complete. This monotonicity theorem also establishes the $s_{n-1}$-to-$s_n$ ratio conjecture posed in recent work on extremal mean subtree order.
